findings.title: Negative slice start in OptimizedCursorPaginator raises on the advanced path
findings.description: When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the new code sets `start_offset = cursor.offset` and runs `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django's `QuerySet.__getitem__` rejects negative slice starts with an `AssertionError` ("Negative indexing is not supported"). Every request on this branch therefore fails with a 500 instead of returning data. The comment "The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" is incorrect. The same unguarded path also applies to `is_prev` cursors in `BasePaginator`, where `start_offset = offset` is passed through unclamped.

findings.title: BasePaginator comment says negative offsets are allowed, but the code clamps them
findings.description: The added comment says the change allows negative offsets for bidirectional pagination. The code does the opposite for non-prev cursors: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` silently clamps negative offsets to 0. For `is_prev` cursors it passes them through unclamped, which hits the slicing failure described above. The comment does not describe what the code does, and the two branches behave inconsistently.
